active_problem.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07/F-05).
Of 3,025 disputed bills, 1,240 (41%) were on ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 (59%) were on ACTUAL reads (E-04/F-04), so the known estimate-substitution mechanism explains only part of the surge.
active_problem.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets at Lakeside Water Utility doubled from ~600/month to ~1,200-1,260/month between July and August-September 2026 (E-07) because manual meter-reading route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target over that window, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts (E-02); the resulting missed field reads trigger estimate substitution in the billing import step, and this substitution channel accounts for the 41% of disputed bills that were on ESTIMATED reads (E-04), producing inaccurate bills that drive a material share of the dispute surge. Response-handling speed is not the mechanism, since dispute response times remain within SLA throughout the surge (E-01).

VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What causes the 59% majority of disputed bills that were on ACTUAL reads (not estimate substitution) - a billing import validation rule change (H-RULES-CHANGE) or AMI data delivery degradation (H-AMI-DATA-DEGRADED)?

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data (2440 tickets) shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA — ticket response handling is already meeting its service target. This speaks only to response speed, not to whether underlying bills are correct or to the volume doubling itself.

Field route-log data (COMPLETE, AUTHORITATIVE) shows manual-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — a material shortfall in field read collection during the exact window the dispute surge began.

billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/rate change was logged around the dispute surge window — the system of record shows no legitimate rate change event that could explain customers' bills changing.

billing-db shows 3025 disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED / 1785 ACTUAL; estimate substitution (the mechanism behind the AMI-degraded and field-staffing hypotheses) can account for at most the 41% tied to ESTIMATED reads, while the 59% majority of disputes were on bills already using ACTUAL reads, implying an additional error source beyond read-type substitution.
